key_insight: Generative AI can represent multiple plausible turbulent flows, but physical fidelity requires validation beyond visual realism, pointwise error, and low-order spectra.
engineering_relevance: Potential applications include stochastic closures, flow super-resolution, data assimilation, and uncertainty quantification when observations or resolved scales are incomplete.
method: Review diffusion models, score-based methods, and probability-transport formulations.
Examine flow generation, probabilistic reconstruction, reduced-order modeling, and temporal evolution.
Propose physics-aware validation and a reproducible benchmark ecosystem.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports no quantitative benchmark results; it calls for evaluation of energy transfer, intermittency, conservation, temporal consistency, ensemble diversity, and generalization.
watch_item: Limited data, weak baselines, and incomplete validation can obscure whether generated flows capture turbulent physics rather than merely resemble training examples.
paper_title: Generative AI in Turbulence: Foundations, Applications, Validations and Benchmarks
